subject.title: Manage Claw cron jobs through the gateway

question: Should the Claws RFC adopt durable Gateway-owned cron declarations while also making generic agent deletion resumable or fail-closed whenever cron teardown cannot be completed?
rationale: The PR expands an experimental Claws contract into unconditional generic agent-deletion behavior, and choosing between a durable cross-owner deletion operation, a narrower Claw-only slice, or pausing the feature is a product and ownership decision rather than a mechanical repair.

options.title: Require durable deletion
options.body: Keep the Gateway-owned design, but require resumable cron and agent teardown plus explicit offline behavior and live proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow to Claw cleanup
options.body: Remove the generic `agents.delete` extension from this slice and retain only Claw-owned cron lifecycle behavior until canonical deletion is designed separately.

options.title: Pause the cron slice
options.body: Hold this stacked PR until the RFC settles scheduler ownership, deletion atomicity, and offline recovery semantics.

recommendation.title: Require durable deletion
recommendation.body: Keep the Gateway-owned design, but require resumable cron and agent teardown plus explicit offline behavior and live proof before merge.
